title: Positive-temperature order in the three-dimensional Edwards–Anderson spin glass
aliases: positive overlap broadening in short-range spin glasses
decision_reason: The source-defined finite-temperature overlap question passes current-result comparisons, independent status corroboration, baseline duplicate review and a separated adversarial draft pass. No later matching resolution located as of September 17, 2026.

problem_fingerprint.model_or_objects: Ising spins with quenched independent Gaussian nearest-neighbor bonds and two independent thermal replicas of the same disorder
problem_fingerprint.boundary_or_initial_conditions: Free boundary; no external field; zero replica coupling
problem_fingerprint.parameter_range: All fixed beta>beta_0 for some finite beta_0>0
problem_fingerprint.quantifiers: Exists finite beta_0; for every beta>beta_0 the disorder-averaged squared site overlap has positive limsup
problem_fingerprint.normalization: Hamiltonian -sum_unordered_edges J_e sigma_x sigma_y; R=L^(-3)sum_sites sigma_x^1 sigma_x^2; Boltzmann factor exp(-beta H)
problem_fingerprint.observable_or_norm: E_J expectation under product Gibbs measure of R^2
problem_fingerprint.limit_regime_and_order: Fix beta finite; then limsup L->infinity. No beta->infinity before volume limit.
problem_fingerprint.requested_conclusion: Strictly positive overlap broadening at sufficiently low positive temperature
problem_fingerprint.computational_model_and_dependencies: Equilibrium phase question; no numerical evidence or mean-field approximation assumed

statement_source_and_scope_match: IMT §3.1 explicitly states the low-temperature expectation for d>=3 and defines the open-boundary, uncoupled-replica broadening parameter by limsup in Eq. (3.3). We use d=3 and the standard Gaussian law permitted by §2.1 and independently specified by NS and CHAT. Positivity of the displayed limsup is exactly q_br>0.
proposed_statement_text: For the nearest-neighbor Ising Edwards–Anderson model on [1,L]^3 with free boundary, zero field and independent N(0,1) bonds, does there exist finite beta_0 such that limsup_{L->infinity} E_J <(L^(-3) sum_x sigma_x^1 sigma_x^2)^2>_{beta,J}^{tensor 2}>0 for every beta>beta_0?
applied_significance: A model of a magnet with frustrated, frozen random interactions. Nonzero overlap fluctuations indicate that two equilibrated replicas retain macroscopic common spin structure, even though spin-flip symmetry makes the signed mean overlap zero.

duplicate_review.distinctness_reason: Neither baseline nor accepted additions has this positive-temperature short-range disordered overlap assertion.
implications_or_equivalences: All versions of the same low-temperature order question remain one canonical entry.
Positive q_br implies positive q_EA by IMT, but the converse is not claimed.
No claim about replica symmetry breaking beyond global spin-flip structure is included.

open_status_evidence_summary: IMT identifies expected low-temperature order and characterizes it without proving positivity. NS independently poses the phase-transition question; HK §3.1 says the 3D finite-temperature transition remains unproved. CHAT v6 gives only zero-temperature results.
independent_status_corroboration: NS, HK and CHAT have no authors in common with IMT. HK provides 2025 published status corroboration, while CHAT May 2026 explicitly limits its scope to zero temperature.
strongest_known_partial_results_and_gap: IMT proves q_EA>=q_br, conditional on overlap broadening rather than its positivity. CHAT establishes several rigorous ground-state glassy signatures. Neither establishes nonzero q_br at any finite beta in three dimensions.

issues_found: Need finite beta before volume limit, and limsup rather than unsupported existence of a limit.
Two replicas must use the same disorder.
Site overlap differs from bond overlap, and zero-field variance equals second moment only through spin-flip symmetry.
Do not infer replica symmetry breaking or equality q_EA=q_br.
issues_resolved: Checked against IMT §§2–3; all conventions explicit.
Fixed finite beta and product Gibbs law at fixed J stated.
IS v2 positive-field hypothesis and explicit zero-field limitation checked.
No extra structural claim about the spin-glass phase added.
Baseline 195 and 196 reread and distinctness confirmed.
